articles.title: High Court decision means landlord licensing will go ahead
articles.summary: The High Court has for the second time  dismissed a judicial review of Thurrock council’s Selective Licensing Scheme. The claimant had sought an oral hearing to challenge the High Court’s previous written decision to dismiss the claim on March 13 this year.  That decision allowed the authority to start to implement the scheme. The court has […]
articles.ai_summary:
- The High Court has upheld Thurrock council's Selective Licensing Scheme by dismissing a judicial review, allowing implementation to proceed.
- This marks the second rejection of challenges against the licensing scheme, reaffirming the council's authority to regulate landlords in the area.

articles.title: Council probe and court case ends with small fine for landlord
articles.summary: A council investigation into an HMO has ended with a court case and the landlord paying just £1,145 in fines and costs. Erewash council launched its prosecution of landlord Mahmood Rahemtulla after he ignored a request to supply documentation about tenancy agreements and rent deposits at the five-bed house in Long Eaton. The council also […]
articles.ai_summary:
- Erewash Council prosecutes landlord Mahmood Rahemtulla for failing to provide tenancy documentation for a five-bed HMO, culminating in a court case.  
- The outcome: Rahemtulla fined a mere £1,145 for his non-compliance with regulatory requests.
